ASIAN GREEN BEE EATER.habitat: Open grasslands, agricultural fields, scrublands and woodland edges.
ASIAN GREEN BEE EATER.distribution: South Asia, Southeast Asia and parts of the Middle East.
ASIAN GREEN BEE EATER.diet: Bees, wasps, dragonflies, butterflies and other flying insects.
ASIAN GREEN BEE EATER.physical_characteristics: Small, slender green bird with a black eye stripe, pointed bill and elongated central tail feathers.

CASPIAN TERN.habitat: Coastal lagoons, estuaries, lakes and large inland water bodies.
CASPIAN TERN.distribution: Widely distributed across parts of North America, Europe, Asia, Africa and Oceania.
CASPIAN TERN.diet: Primarily fish, caught by diving into water.
CASPIAN TERN.physical_characteristics: Large tern with a powerful red bill, black cap, pale body and long pointed wings.

DARK EYED JUNCO.habitat: Coniferous forests, woodland edges, gardens and open areas.
DARK EYED JUNCO.distribution: North America, including Canada, the United States and parts of Mexico.
DARK EYED JUNCO.diet: Seeds, grains, berries and small insects.
DARK EYED JUNCO.physical_characteristics: Small sparrow-like bird with a rounded head, short pink bill and contrasting dark and pale plumage.

EASTERN YELLOW ROBIN.habitat: Woodlands, forests, rainforest edges and coastal scrub.
EASTERN YELLOW ROBIN.diet: Insects, spiders and other small invertebrates.
EASTERN YELLOW ROBIN.physical_characteristics: Small bird with a bright yellow underside, grey upperparts and a dark bill.

GREY HEADED CHACHALACA.habitat: Tropical forests, forest edges, secondary woodland and dense vegetation.
GREY HEADED CHACHALACA.distribution: Central America, particularly from Honduras through Panama.
GREY HEADED CHACHALACA.physical_characteristics: Medium-sized, long-tailed bird with a greyish head, brownish body and relatively small head crest.

HOUSE FINCH.habitat: Urban areas, gardens, farms, deserts and open woodland.
HOUSE FINCH.distribution: North America, including the United States and Mexico.
HOUSE FINCH.diet: Seeds, fruits and occasionally small insects.
HOUSE FINCH.physical_characteristics: Small finch with a short conical bill. Males commonly have reddish coloration around the head and breast.

JACOBIN PIGEON.habitat: Domestic environments, aviaries and managed pigeon lofts.
JACOBIN PIGEON.distribution: Kept domestically in many countries worldwide.
JACOBIN PIGEON.diet: Seeds, grains and commercially prepared pigeon feed.
JACOBIN PIGEON.physical_characteristics: Distinctive domestic pigeon breed with a large hood of feathers surrounding the head and neck.
JACOBIN PIGEON.conservation_status: Domestic breed; wild IUCN conservation status is not applicable.

LAUGHING GULL.habitat: Coastal beaches, marshes, estuaries, islands and shorelines.
LAUGHING GULL.distribution: Atlantic and Gulf coasts of North America, Central America and the Caribbean.
LAUGHING GULL.diet: Fish, insects, crustaceans, molluscs and discarded food.
LAUGHING GULL.physical_characteristics: Medium-sized gull with a dark hood during breeding season, grey wings and a red bill.

LIMPKIN.habitat: Freshwater marshes, swamps, wetlands and vegetated lake edges.
LIMPKIN.distribution: Southeastern United States, Central America, the Caribbean and South America.
LIMPKIN.diet: Primarily freshwater snails, especially apple snails.
LIMPKIN.physical_characteristics: Large wading bird with brown plumage, white markings and a long, slightly curved bill.

MERLIN.habitat: Open woodland, grasslands, coastal areas and open landscapes.
MERLIN.distribution: North America, Europe and northern Asia, with seasonal migration.
MERLIN.diet: Small birds, insects and occasionally small mammals.
MERLIN.physical_characteristics: Small, compact falcon with pointed wings, a short tail and rapid flight.

OVENBIRD.habitat: Mature deciduous and mixed forests with leaf-covered ground.
OVENBIRD.distribution: Breeds in eastern and northern North America and winters in Central America and the Caribbean.
OVENBIRD.diet: Insects, spiders, worms and other small invertebrates.
OVENBIRD.physical_characteristics: Olive-brown upperparts, white underside with dark streaks and an orange crown stripe bordered by dark lines.

OYSTER CATCHER.habitat: Coastal shorelines, mudflats, sandy beaches and rocky intertidal areas.
OYSTER CATCHER.distribution: Oystercatcher species occur along coastlines worldwide.
OYSTER CATCHER.diet: Molluscs, shellfish, marine worms and other coastal invertebrates.
OYSTER CATCHER.physical_characteristics: Typically a robust shorebird with a long, strong bill, often bright red or orange, and contrasting plumage.

RED KNOT.habitat: Coastal mudflats, sandy beaches, tidal flats and tundra breeding grounds.
RED KNOT.distribution: Arctic breeding regions with long-distance migrations to coastal areas worldwide.
RED KNOT.diet: Molluscs, small crustaceans, worms and other invertebrates.
RED KNOT.physical_characteristics: Medium-sized migratory shorebird with a straight bill and reddish breeding plumage.

RED TAILED HAWK.habitat: Open fields, deserts, grasslands, forests and mountainous areas.
RED TAILED HAWK.distribution: North America and parts of Central America and the Caribbean.
RED TAILED HAWK.diet: Small mammals, birds, reptiles and other small animals.
RED TAILED HAWK.physical_characteristics: Large bird of prey with broad wings, a hooked bill and a characteristic reddish tail in adults.

SORA.habitat: Freshwater marshes, wetlands and shallow vegetated water bodies.
SORA.distribution: North America, migrating to Central America and the Caribbean during winter.
SORA.diet: Seeds, aquatic plants, insects and small aquatic invertebrates.
SORA.physical_characteristics: Small rail with a short yellow bill, dark face and grey breast.

VIOLET BACKED STARLING.habitat: Woodlands, savannas, forest edges and open wooded habitats.
VIOLET BACKED STARLING.diet: Primarily fruits and berries, along with insects.
VIOLET BACKED STARLING.physical_characteristics: Male has glossy violet upperparts and white underparts; female is brown and streaked.

VIOLET GREEN SWALLOW.habitat: Open woodlands, mountain areas, cliffs and areas near water.
VIOLET GREEN SWALLOW.distribution: Western North America, migrating to Mexico and Central America.
VIOLET GREEN SWALLOW.physical_characteristics: Small streamlined swallow with iridescent green and violet upperparts and white underparts.

WOOD DUCK.habitat: Wooded swamps, freshwater marshes, ponds and forested wetlands.
WOOD DUCK.diet: Seeds, acorns, aquatic plants, fruits and insects.
WOOD DUCK.physical_characteristics: Colorful perching duck. Males have an iridescent green head, chestnut breast and distinctive white markings.

WOOD THRUSH.habitat: Moist deciduous forests with dense understory and leaf litter.
WOOD THRUSH.distribution: Eastern North America, migrating to Central America during winter.
WOOD THRUSH.physical_characteristics: Medium-sized songbird with warm brown upperparts, a white breast and dark round spots.

YELLOW BREASTED CHAT.habitat: Dense shrubs, thickets, forest edges and overgrown fields.
YELLOW BREASTED CHAT.distribution: North America, migrating to Mexico and Central America.
YELLOW BREASTED CHAT.physical_characteristics: Large warbler-like bird with a bright yellow breast, olive-green upperparts, white spectacles and a long tail.
